              its detail panel says it is stale.
style: box-sizing: border-box; color: #AFB5C5; font-family: Poppins, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0px; line-height: 18px; text-align: left; width: 100%

name: Task status rules
text:
Running / monitoring / review: purple pulse. Needs you: amber pulse. Done: green.
              Failed: red. Queued / cancelled: neutral. Scheduled retry: amber, still. Waiting on
              workers: purple, still.
style: box-sizing: border-box; color: #AFB5C5; font-family: Poppins, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0px; line-height: 18px; text-align: left; width: 100%

name: Reference precedence
text:
One chip: PR first, otherwise issue. Keep a different issue number in the title.
              Conflict takes over the chip; the underlying PR status remains in its detail panel.
style: box-sizing: border-box; color: #AFB5C5; font-family: Poppins, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0px; line-height: 18px; text-align: left; width: 100%

name: Responsive behavior
text:
Proposed two-line row keeps the title readable at narrow widths. Task and tracker are
          separate targets. Desktop hover/focus reveals tracker details; touch opens the tracker
          directly. Preserve queue position; hide age when a reference is present. Pulse is a
          runtime behavior, shown statically here.
